r4e-crew-context-newline.title: Inherited rule: CREW_CONTEXT 'Writing Files On Windows'
r4e-crew-context-newline.imperative: CREW_CONTEXT mandates newline='\n' on every write. Judge whether the new save(), which may deliberately write CRLF, complies with that documented standard or departs from it.
r4e-crew-context-newline.finding: Complies with the standard's INTENT and with its own second paragraph; departs from the literal wording. CREW_CONTEXT 'Writing Files On Windows' says pass encoding='utf-8', newline='\n' on EVERY write, and names two hazards: a non-UTF-8 default encoding and default CRLF translation. The new save() eliminates both more strongly than the prescribed mechanism does -- it encodes explicitly to UTF-8 and writes BYTES, so no translation layer exists at all. And the same CREW_CONTEXT section's next paragraph says '.gitattributes sets * text=auto, so a checkout may legitimately hold CRLF while the blob holds LF', which is a direct argument FOR preserving a legitimately-CRLF checkout rather than forcing LF. Confirmed the premise against the world: core.autocrlf=true and .gitattributes '* text=auto' in this repo; the working-tree engine file holds 2883 CRLF / 0 LF while the HEAD blob holds 0 CRLF / 2827 LF. OBSERVATION, not a blocker: a reader applying CREW_CONTEXT literally would read save() as violating it, and CREW_CONTEXT does not name the engine's preservation policy as the sanctioned exception. CREW_CONTEXT is outside this issue's allowed scope, so this is a triage candidate rather than rework. The implementer's Map Impact claim that save() 'honors' this section is substantially right on intent and loose on letter -- not a materially wrong graph-impact claim.
